real_qa.q: What is title insurance and why is it required for commercial real estate transactions?
real_qa.r: Title insurance proves ownership of a property and protects against unknown liens, unpaid taxes, and other encumbrances. Banks require title insurance as collateral protection because they are assuming the majority of the risk in a transaction. The title company conducts research to determine who owns the property, whether taxes and deeds of trust have been paid off, and identifies easements or restrictions that may affect property use.
real_qa.requete: what is title insurance why required

real_qa.q: How far back does title insurance research go for commercial properties in Washington state?
real_qa.r: For commercial properties in Washington, title insurance research goes back to 1889, when Washington became a state. This marks the line in the sand where recording rules were codified and government patents were established. Everything from 1889 forward is searchable and the title company is responsible for those documents.

real_qa.q: What is a legal description in a property title report and what forms can it take?
real_qa.r: A legal description is a definition of a piece of property that can be verified on record with the county. Simple descriptions use lot and block notation like 'Lot one, block two of Smith's Addition.' More complex descriptions use meets and bounds format which can be five pages long for larger acreage, or government survey descriptions, all describing the exact boundaries of the property.

real_qa.q: What does 'clear off' mean in a title report and how are recorded liens removed?
real_qa.r: To 'clear off' means to remove a paragraph or risk from the title report by discovering payoff information and filing a reconveyance document. When a deed of trust is paid off, a formal document called a reconveyance must be filed to remove the lien from title. If the original bank has been sold or closed, obtaining the payoff records can be challenging, but once obtained, the reconveyance can be filed to eliminate the risk.
real_qa.requete: clear off title report deed of trust reconveyance

real_qa.q: What is vesting in a property title and why does it matter for commercial real estate transactions?
real_qa.r: Vesting means determining who owns the property, which could be an individual, married couple, LLC, or corporation. Each entity type has different rules for how they can transfer title, so title companies request charter documents like LLC operating agreements to ensure the correct parties have capacity to sign documents. For example, if a property is titled to both Bob and Mary Smith but only Bob signs the purchase agreement, the transaction cannot proceed until both owners authorize it.
